title: probe orchestration lab scratchpad
content:
Quick context: this is a working scratchpad for a small lab focused on the orchestration of short, high-signal probes used to validate cross-functional rollout assumptions for LLM features. 

Purpose:
- Capture minimal viable probe patterns (low-friction canaries + short A/B probes) that product, SRE, and applied-ML teams can spin up repeatedly.
- Emphasize observability-first decisions so we can make quick rollback decisions without heavy manual analysis.
- Define a lightweight stewarding choreography (who watches, who pauses, who escalates).

Goals for this doc:
1) Produce 3 reusable probe templates (latency-sensitive, quality-sensitive, cost-bound).
2) Standardize signal thresholds and action mappings for each template.
3) Lay out a coordination checklist for cross-team pause/rollback.

Definitions (lab jargon):
- Probe: short-lived traffic partition with targeted metrics to test a hypothesis (often 0.5%–5% of traffic; can be synthetic).
- Probe steward: on-duty engineer/product person responsible for watching signals and executing rollback.
- Canary: longer-duration probe intended for operational validation across high-fidelity traffic slices.

Probe templates (sketches)
1) Latency probe (fast-fail hypothesis)
   - Objective: confirm no p99 regression > 250ms for interactive endpoints under typical load.
   - Slice: 1% of active web UI traffic (canary cookie).
   - Duration: 30 minutes steady, 2h monitoring window.
   - Signals: p50/p90/p99 latency, 5xx rate, tail token generation time, autoscaling events.
   - Thresholds: p99 increase > 40% OR 5xx rate > 0.2% => pause.
   - Action: auto-fallback to previous model variant, notify steward channel, start post-mortem ticket.

2) Quality probe (semantic regression hypothesis)
   - Objective: surface user-facing regressions for instruction-following / hallucination.
   - Slice: 0.5% of organic chat requests + 1000 synthetic golden prompts.
   - Duration: 24 hours with daily manual review cadence.
   - Signals: NLU fail rate from evals, user report rate, automated hallucination heuristics, BLEU/ROUGE-like deltas on golden set.
   - Thresholds: automated eval drop > 3% absolute on golden prompts OR user reports > 2x baseline => alert steward.
   - Action: hold rollout, trigger canary-incremental audit by applied-ML, reduce exposure.

3) Cost-bound probe (unit economics check)
   - Objective: verify per-request token cost and latency/cost trade-offs under burst.
   - Slice: staged traffic ramp: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% over 3 hours.
   - Duration: ramp + 6h observation.
   - Signals: tokens-per-session, GPU utilization, request queueing time, cost burn vs forecast.
   - Thresholds: per-request cost > 1.5x forecast OR average GPU utilization > 85% causing queueing => stop ramp.
   - Action: scale dedicated pool or revert model quantization change, notify finance & infra leads.

Telemetry & signal priorities (minimal viable telemetry set)
- Safety-critical (auto actions): 5xx rate, p99 latency, queue length, OOMs, autoscaler kicks.
- Quality signals (human in loop): golden-set delta, user-reports, conversation abort rate, rerank fallback frequency.
- Economy signals (ops/product): tokens/request, per-token cost delta, billing anomaly.

Signal mapping: example mapping that the steward UI should show by default
- Top row: p99 latency / 5xx rate / active canary percentage / golden-set delta
- Mid row: user report rate / avg tokens / GPU queue length
- Bottom row: logs link (tail 1h), trace links (slowest 10), recent commits & model version

Coordination matrix (who does what)
- Probe owner (product PM): hypothesis, success criteria, comms plan.
- Steward (on-call engineer from SRE/product infra): watches auto actions, initiates pause/revert.
- Applied ML owner: investigates quality failures, runs targeted evals.
- Observability owner (console eng): ensures dashboards, synthetic traffic, alerting hooks.
- CS/Support contact: ready to triage user reports if spike in complaints.

Runbook (short form)
1) Start probe: create probe run in Console with tags: probe/lab, owner, hypothesis, linked PR.
2) Auto-monitor: system automatically enforces thresholds for safety-critical signals (auto-fallback).
3) Steward watch: steward picks 30min window to observe earliest signal drift.
4) If auto action occurs: steward confirms, posts to #product-rollouts (template message below), opens post-mortem ticket.
5) If quality signal triggers (non-auto): steward pauses exposure, applied-ML runs golden-set audit within 1h.

Alert & comms template (quick post to channel)
- Title: [PROBE PAUSED] probe-id: latency-probe-20251104
- What: auto-fallback triggered due to p99 latency +45%
- Impact: 1% of web UI traffic reverted to previous model; no user-facing errors observed yet
- Next steps: steward (Omar) investigating; applied-ML assigned Priya to run replay; ETA 2h

Safe defaults and guardrails (lab rules)
- Never expand a probe > 5% without a 24h green window and explicit approvals from SRE and product.
- All probes must include a synthetic golden set for quality probes.
- Auto actions only for safety-critical signals. Quality regressions first require human confirmation.
- Every probe must record linked_artifacts: PRs, JIRA ticket, hypothesis short text.

Data collection & privacy notes
- Ensure synthetic prompts do not include PII.
- For private deployments, hooks should use customer-safe telemetry and only surface deltas (no raw prompts) in public dashboards.

Examples of quick experiments to run in the lab
- Reranker temperature tweak: 0.2 -> 0.1 (quality probe + golden set)
- KV cache warmup behavior: test with synthetic repeat prompts (latency probe)
- Quantization delta for embedded models (cost-bound probe + small A/B)

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self)
- What is the minimum size golden set that reliably detects serious hallucination regressions? (1000 seems high — can we get to 200?)
- How aggressive should auto-fallback thresholds be for p99 in regions with inherently noisy networks (APAC)?
- Where is the line for auto-actions on economy signals vs human-approved changes?
- Can we automate a short snapshot audit (10–50 prompts) that runs within 10 minutes after a probe starts to catch gross regressions early?

Immediate next steps (action list)
- [ ] Build 3 dashboard templates in Console for the probe templates above (obs owner).
- [ ] Wire auto-fallback hooks for p99 / 5xx (infra).
- [ ] Assemble a 200-item candidate golden set focused on hallucination-prone prompts (applied-ML + PM).
- [ ] Create playbook stub in Confluence and link it to the probe run flow (product).

Notes to self / friction points observed in previous runs
- Manual pausing has been slow because steward has to gather trace links by hand — need a Console quick-action that attaches the last 30 slow traces.
- Finance often surprised by temporary burst costs; add optional preflight cost-estimate in probe creation UI.

References and quick links
- rollout-signal-catalog (Confluence)
- canary-telemetry-guidelines (internal doc id: DOC-778)

If you read nothing else: keep probes small, instrumented, and stewarded. The goal is to detect real regressions fast, with minimal blast radius, and with clear ownership for action.
